approved: Public and Educational Lending Rights (Better Income for Authors) Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill makes technical changes and transitional rules that go with a new law on payments to authors when libraries lend their books.
It would repeal the 1985 Act that currently covers public lending rights and shift arrangements to a new scheme set up by a different bill.
The explanatory memorandum does not specify the date these changes start or list every Act amended.
Repeal the Public Lending Right Act 1985.
Provide transitional rules so the old system runs smoothly into the new one.
Allow a new scheme to be created by legislative instrument under the companion bill.
Authors, libraries, and government agencies involved in the public and educational lending rights schemes.
Referred the secrecy provisions bills and the Public and Educational Lending Rights bills to the Federation Chamber for further consideration after the relevant second-reading debates adjourn.

Supported bills consolidating and modernising the Public Lending Right and Educational Lending Right schemes, while noting they do not increase funding or change payment calculations, and called for broader sustained investment to improve Australian authors' incomes.
